name: Fortis Healthcare Ltd
title: Fortis Healthcare Ltd - 532843 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Fortis FY26 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR9,128 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 22.8%; FY27 guidance is 15%+ hospital revenue growth.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR9,128 crores (+17.3%), with hospital revenue up 19.1% to INR7,773 crores and consolidated operating EBITDA up 31.3% to INR2,085 crores (22.8% margin vs 20.4%). Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,365 crores (+17.8%) and PAT rose 44.2% to INR271 crores. Management flagged softer Q4 occupancy at several large hospitals, attributed to a drop in international patients and a government price cap on oncology drugs affecting CGHS/ECHS business in Punjab. Net debt rose to INR2,334 crores (1.09x net debt/EBITDA) on acquisitions and investments.

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR7,773 crores (+19.1%), operating EBITDA margin 22.2% vs 20.5%; ~85% of consolidated revenue and EBITDA. Q4 revenue INR2,023 crores (+19%), Q4 EBITDA margin 22.1%. Occupancy 68% vs 69%; ARPOB up 3.4% to INR2.51 crores.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue INR1,527 crores (+8.5%), operating EBITDA INR360 crores (23.6% margin vs 17.7%; 23.2% ex one-offs). Q4 gross revenue INR387 crores (+11.1%), EBITDA INR85 crores, margin 22%; Q4 tests ~10 million (+5%). Preventive health 13% of mix vs 11%; B2C:B2B 52:48 for FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital revenue growth guided at 15%+ on an ongoing (organic) basis; acquisitions excluded and additive.
FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 150 bps; long-term target of 25% by FY28 reaffirmed, with management seeing 1.5%-2% annual improvement.
Diagnostics FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23%-24%; revenue growth targeted at double digits (currently ~8.5%), with ~70% volume and ~30% value mix.
Jaipur expected to grow ~15% in FY27 with 13%-14% EBITDA margin.
Brownfield bed additions of 500+ in FY27 and ~1,800 beds over the next 4 years; capex about INR900 crores annually (about 60% maintenance).
Dividend of INR1 per share (10% of face value), fourth consecutive year, subject to shareholder approval.
IHH reportedly plans to raise stake to 50% and infuse ~INR10,000 crores fresh equity; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR700 crores; ~250 beds added via brownfield (Manesar, Noida, Faridabad) and ~800 beds added in total including acquisitions.

Acquired People Tree Hospital (125 beds, Bengaluru, Jan 2026) with land for 300+ beds; Shrimann Super Specialty Jalandhar (228 beds, Jul 2025) with land for 450+ beds; 200-bed Greater Noida lease (Sep 2025); Adayu 36-bed mental health facility in Gurugram (Nov 2025).
FMRI new tower to be operationalised within about a week, opening ~100 beds in FY27 on a phased basis; FY27 brownfield additions of 400+ beds per earlier statement, with 500+ per later remark.
Shalimar Bagh expansion delayed pending approvals; ~300 beds moved from FY28 to FY29; Mohali, Shalimar Bagh and Amritsar large towers ~2.5-3 years away.
BG Road has ~100 beds of brownfield capacity uncommissioned until occupancy improves; Mulund considering another tower.
demand_pricing: Hospital occupancy 68% in FY26 vs 69%; occupied beds up 15% (management cited 3,270 to 2,838, a figure order inverted in the transcript). FMRI at 85-95% occupancy; BG Road at ~55% vs ~63-64% area norm.
International patient revenue +18.5% to INR639 crores (7.8% of hospital revenue); Q4 international growth ~11%. Management is diversifying to Africa and other markets.
Oncology drug price capping (~30% of MRP) under CGHS/ECHS led Fortis to stop some high-cost drug cases, mainly in Punjab; no timeline for resolution. Management said margin impact is limited.
Focus specialties grew 18.9% and make up 62% of hospital revenue; radiation therapy volumes +19%, robotic surgeries +66%.
Diagnostics: 40.8 million tests in FY26 vs 39.2 million; 50+ new tests added; Illumina NovaSeq X operational at Mumbai reference lab.

qa_highlights.question: Why are occupancies falling at large hospitals such as FMRI and BG Road, and how will this improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal attributed the drop mainly to lower international business (Q4 growth ~11% vs 18-20% for the year) and oncology drug capping in Punjab. He said BG Road is low due to TPA/cash mix, intense competition and a 55% level versus a 63-64% area norm, with a target above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand given new capacity and doctor cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashutosh Raghuvanshi said doctor costs rose slightly but further increases are not expected; the 25% FY28 margin target is intact, with 1.5-2% annual improvement now seen as more confident.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did the 800 new beds contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Q4 hospital revenue of INR2,000 crores would be INR1,928 crores excluding People Tree, Adayu and Jalandhar, so new-unit contribution is small.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA of Gleneagles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not consolidate Gleneagles and does not track full-year numbers; it is trending around INR70 per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is Diagnostics demerger being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the focus is on profitability, this is not the time to lock value, and alternatives may be considered once the business matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Gleneagles transaction moving forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is under deliberation and evaluation; no timeline, and it would need majority-of-minority approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Manesar run-rate and FMRI ARPOB driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar FY26 revenue was INR140 crores at ~48% occupancy (new beds being added) and reached EBITDA breakeven. FMRI ARPOB rise was attributed to gross-basis international business, MR Linac, Gamma Knife and day-care oncology.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Jaipur and FEHI improving, and why build a Bangalore hospital in a competitive market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operational efficiency, new facilities and clinical talent at FEHI; Jaipur expected to grow ~15% at 13-14% margin. The People Tree site is a less competitive micro-market with underserved catchment, per Ashutosh Raghuvanshi.

risks_watch: Oncology drug price caps under CGHS/ECHS and the pace of revenue loss in Punjab, with no resolution timeline.
Occupancy at large hospitals (FMRI, BG Road, Faridabad) and absorption of new beds in Gurgaon and Noida amid doctor cost pressure.
International patient growth slowing (Q4 ~11%) and sustainability of domestic growth offsetting it.
Shalimar Bagh approval delays moving ~300 beds from FY28 to FY29.
Debt rise to 1.09x net debt/EBITDA after acquisitions; FY27 capex about INR900 crores.
Pending Gleneagles transaction and IHH equity infusion, both without timelines.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year financials and FY27 guidance, reaffirming the 25% FY28 hospital margin target. Cautious and evasive on the oncology pricing issue, Gleneagles, IHH capital and some occupancy questions, giving no timelines or figures where they were requested.
key_quotes: If at all, we are more confident now that we can continue to deliver this progress every year, at least to 1.5% to 2% year-on-year.
So revenue-wise, we are well poised to see on hospital side, 15% plus revenue growth.
And I think this is not the right time to do any sort of value locking at this point.
